hook: Picture a cheerful children's science show whose host knows far too much about anomalies and the Foundation. The transcript and episode table play the format completely straight, laugh track and all, so read it as a parody of educational TV with very real consequences attached.
whyItMatters: SCP-2702 has no object to lock away; what needs containing is a broadcast whose origin keeps shifting and episodes that surface online. Its comedy comes from the gap between the show's breezy tone, with its reminders to ask a parent first, and the cost when researchers copy its experiments. It also turns the Foundation's documentation habits into part of the joke, down to a requested format for logging newly found episodes.
thingsToNotice:
The memetics episode tests a hop-on-one-foot agent on the robot co-host, finds him immune, and turns it on the viewers instead, and Foundation tests confirm it works on real audiences. The episode table escalates from alien specimens and a teleportation booth to a summoning ritual whose recreation caused a breach and full lockdown of Site 64 with 27 casualties, after which repeating any experiment needs level 4 authorization.

The seventh episode sneaks through Site-24 with accurate details and identifiable staff, exaggerating only the guards' incompetence, and even teaches how to format an SCP report. The eighth simulates an impact that always ends in a GH-class Dead Greenhouse scenario within a month, and Foundation astronomers then actually locate the redacted object, unable to estimate whether it will hit. The credits list Doctor Wondertainment among the sponsors.
